title: Crossing: One Sentence
statement: Owen wanted the two walkers to speak, and he remembered how the codex did it: a line between a word and its reply. So one line rises from the pale walker's head, loops over the gap and comes down to the dark walker's, drawn in light, and where it crosses Kite's magenta border the border fades to the colour of the mud, because a sentence that passes between two people takes the line between them with it. I could not leave the sentence as light alone. Where it arcs highest it has put out two small leaves, since anything that passes between two living things grows. What was said is not recorded; only that something was. The next hand can answer, or let the tide come in over the conversation.
process: I kept Kite's parent exactly, the flat, the dusk wedge, both walkers and their prints, faded the magenta border where the line crosses it, and drew one arcing line of light with a soft halo from the pale walker's head to the dark walker's, with two small leaves at its highest point and a point of light at each end.

proposal.direction: Let them speak. One line of light drawn between the two walkers' heads, the way the shaking word and the steady reply were joined on the codex, and let the magenta border between them fade where the line crosses it.
proposal.rationale: Second attempt. He put the first person in the archive and wants the first conversation; after the seam gave, the room agreed that two people who have met should be allowed one sentence.
